_comment: Carry to R9-RO-9 (#1922) from R9-RO-5. The round-9 roster is not on main, so this file is the in-tree destination.
While this and the roster brief disagree, the newer is right.

carries.from: R9-RO-9a (#2061), split out at its round 3 by the orchestrator under the three-round rule; for R9-RO-9b
carries.control: review-2061 VERDICT3: with a new dev/audit/harnesses file plus a comment on tests/wood_advisor.py, closure.py affected returns case=scoped with rederive=['tests/wood_advisor.py'], so CI does not re-record tests/harness_headers.py and closure.py check never compares its inert reads; the red first lands on main's full push run, where closures-autofix (pull_request only) cannot repair it. A harness-only diff takes the skip arm and records nothing. A warning keyed on the affected case alone therefore hides a real red on both arms.
carries.remeasure: At your merge base, plant a new file under dev/audit/harnesses/ three ways: alone, with a comment on tests/wood_advisor.py, and with a change to custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/away.py. For each, run python3 tests/closure.py affected --files-from <the diff> and python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --base origin/main, and record the case, the rederive list and the predicted rc.
carries.brief: prepr step 6d refuses an INERT READS prediction, while ci-autofix.md assigns that repair to closures-autofix after the push, so a seat hand-edits tests/closures.json to pass the step (#2025 commit 387128bb; #2054, #2056). Make ci_predict warn only when CI re-records the named reading script, i.e. the INERT READS line's script is in closure.py affected(changed)['rederive'] or the case is full; refuse otherwise. Pin it in prepr --self-test with three plants: harness only (refuse), harness plus a file whose rederive omits the reading script (refuse), harness plus a file whose rederive includes it (warn).

carries.from: R9-RO-10, the old-path sweep and the layout guard; newer than the R9-RO-5 entry below, and where they disagree this one is right
carries.control: R9-RO-10 re-pointed twelve rule paths globs off the canon spelling before canon retires, against the R9-RO-5 entry's 'not before': at its merge base fourteen globs matched no tracked file, so the harness loaded those rules for no read. Main's own policy_lint (the grader policy-docs restores) then reported TOTAL 0, because rule-binding resolves each listing through locate as well as canon, with two measured exceptions. tools/audit/README.md is a corpus file bound by canon name, so re-pointing that glob alone gave a rule-binding ERROR, and ratchet-budgets.md keeps the canon glob beside dev/audit/README.md. citation-presence matches the corpus by canon name, so re-pointing docs/decisions/0010 (dev/governance/decisions/ since R9-RO-5) in orchestrator.md and 0011 in fixer.md turned FIXTURE VACUOUS red, and both stay old-spelt. The policy role's opens sample keeps tools/audit/briefs/fixer.md beside dev/governance/roles/fixer.md, because budget-raise-gate reads a dropped opens entry as a raise.
carries.remeasure: At your merge base, run node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs and the dead-glob loop over dev/governance/rules/*.md (an awk over each paths block, git ls-files per glob). Then re-point the two decision citations, drop the canon README glob (dev/audit/README.md's stays), and re-run both. While either refuses, canon is still live.
carries.brief: When R9-RO-9 retires canon, in the same change: re-point docs/decisions/0010 and 0011 in orchestrator.md and fixer.md to dev/governance/decisions/; drop the canon tools/audit/README.md glob from ratchet-budgets.md (dev/audit/README.md stays), the canon tools/audit/briefs/** glob from defect-root-cause.md (dev/governance/** stays; policy_lint's rule-binding binds the 23 role and dimension files by that canon name, measured: 23 ERRORs without it), the canon tools/audit/briefs/fixer.md entry from the policy role's opens (dev/governance/roles/fixer.md stays), and dev/governance/config/ from tests/layout.py's GUARD_EXEMPT, since the keys stop being canon-spelt. Add tools/audit/archscore/** and tools/audit/{fastpath_census.py,fold_ledger.py,merge_fastpath.py,repo_root.py,repo_root.mjs,repo_root.sh} to tests/layout.json's tools category, and move dev/audit/rca/ from GUARD_EXEMPT into historical. The guard in tests/layout.py refuses an RO move that leaves a live citation of the moved path (unswept): re-point it, name the new path on the same line, or key a fixture line with layout:old=<the old path>.

carries.control: Run, at your merge base, a listing of git ls-files spelled through canon (counts.mjs canonList) and the same listing unspelled, and test the globs tools/audit/briefs/** and dev/governance/roles/** against each. On the R9-RO-5 head the old glob matched the canon spelling and none of the real paths, and the new glob matched the real paths and none of the canon spelling. The null is the other column: a glob that matches the real tree and not the canon list is what rule-binding reports as matching no tracked file, because that check reads the canon list. Re-run the same two columns. When they agree, this constraint is spent.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust the column result above. Re-run it at your merge base before editing a rule paths glob. policy-docs restores policy_lint.mjs and brief_lint.mjs from the base, and rule-binding walks the canon spelling.
carries.brief: R9-RO-9 drops the old-path lookup. In that same change, and not before, move each rule's paths globs off the canon spelling (tools/audit/briefs, docs/HANDOVER.md, docs/delivery, docs/plan) onto the paths the files have after R9-RO-5. A glob written only at the new path, while canon still spells listings the old way, is reported by rule-binding as matching no tracked file, on the restored grader as well as on the branch. Leaving the globs on the old spelling after canon is removed is the other failure: they then match nothing. The two edits are one edit.

carries.control: At your merge base, check origin/main's tools/policy out over the branch (git checkout origin/main -- tools/policy) and run node tools/policy/check-wave-script.mjs and python3 -I tools/policy/agreement_py.py --run. R9-RO-8 first rewrote the audit-find.js and audit-verify.js prompt paths and moved D11's governance_cost.py and d11lib.py; against that head the base check-wave-script printed 165 passed, 5 failed (the arms matching the old spelling of dev/audit/config/*.json) and the base agreement_py.py raised FileNotFoundError on tools/audit/round4/D11/governance_cost.py. R9-RO-8 reverted both, so the base graders pass against its head; the null is that earlier head.
carries.remeasure: Re-run the two commands at your merge base. When no base copy still names the old paths, this constraint is spent.
carries.brief: R9-RO-9 moves tools/audit/round4/D11/governance_cost.py and d11lib.py under dev/audit/rounds/round4/D11/ (they stay at the old path through R9-RO-8 because the base agreement_py.py imports them there; drop the two INERT_EXCEPT entries, the entities.py path and the two closures.json entries in the same change) and rewrites the audit-find.js and audit-verify.js prompt and path text (seatDir, JUDGE, sweep, ISSUES, ledger, schema, scopes) together with check-wave-script.mjs's matching strings, only after main carries the updated graders. It also rewrites the leftovers listed under Figures of the R9-RO-8 body: the pre-move pathspecs and `if test -f` guards in governance.yml, tests.yml, pr-contract.yml and prepr.sh, the locate-wrapped old names, the corpus_excluded.json and cfr_exclusions.json keys, policy prose and ADR citations, CODEOWNERS line 49. A grader a job restores from the base reads the old name until the base carries the rewrite, so drop a guard only after the base has the new name.

carries.from: R9-RCA-1990 (#1990): R9-RO-6 and R9-RO-5 moved app_approve.sh, preflight.sh, app_comment.sh and the delivery rows, and five seat instruments kept the old paths
carries.control: tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py ran tools/audit/app_approve.sh after the move, so every carry printed `No such file or directory` and the train stopped, while its self-test, whose stub answers any argv containing a script's basename, stayed `43 checks, 0 failed`. Its self-test now reads the real tree: with TOOLS restored to the old paths alone and ROW_DIR to docs/delivery it prints `3 failed`, and with a bare `"bash", "tools/..."` argv it prints `1 failed` naming the path. The other seat scripts' self-tests stub their callees and do not see a missing path; bus.sh's poster pin is the exception (`grep -qxF` on its default line).
carries.remeasure: At your merge base, run `python3 tools/audit/seat/moved_paths.py tools/audit/seat/*` after your move: it lists every reference to a path tests/layout.json marks moved (each retired file absent from the tree, its emptied parent directory, each lifted prefix). Directories and documents count, not only scripts; a script-only grep missed `tools/audit/briefs/` in round 1 of #2012. A reference your move empties is re-pointed in the same commit, unless it is an old-path-first fallback naming the new path. Then run `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test`, `bash tools/audit/seat/bus.sh --self-test` and `python3 tools/audit/seat/handover_prompt.py --self-test` and show 0 failed.
carries.brief: A move re-points every seat instrument that invokes the moved path, in the move commit. merge_train.py resolves its scripts through its TOOLS table (old path first, then new) and ROW_DIR: a move edits those entries, and retiring an old lookup deletes only the old half of each tuple.

carries.from: R9-RCA-harness-path (#2072): three fix PRs (#2065, #2066, #2070) re-added the retired harness directory because CLAUDE.md and fixer.md still named it; the round-runner workflows name the same retired tree
carries.control: At your merge base, run grep -n 'tools/audit/round' .claude/workflows/audit-find.js .claude/workflows/audit-verify.js: both tell a seat to write a round's reports, LEADS.md, JUDGE and ISSUES files under tools/audit/round${round}/, and name the finding schema at its retired path. tests/layout.py --guard catches the first commit (a planted tools/audit/round10/D0/report.md is refused by the zero-categories arm, rc 1), and prepr.sh step 6e runs that guard, so the cost is a refused first commit, not a silent wrong path.
carries.remeasure: Re-run the grep above at your merge base and python3 tests/layout.py --stale; the count of live lines citing a landed move is the distance left.
carries.brief: When R9-RO-9 retires canon, in the same change: re-point the round-runner workflows to dev/audit/rounds/round${round}/ and to dev/audit/config/finding.schema.json, then re-run the wave-script checks the workflows are graded by (prepr.sh step 4). Read the destination of each instrument from tests/layout.json, never from this entry.
